title: 3 Ingredient Cloud Bread That Actually Holds Together Without Falling Apart
description: Make airy 3 ingredient cloud bread at home for pennies. Skip the expensive bakery runs with this easy, low-carb US grocery budget recipe.
storyHeading: How to Make This for a Fraction of Takeout Cost
story: If you are tired of spending six bucks on specialty grocery store keto loaves, this quick 3 ingredient cloud bread is your ultimate weeknight sanity saver. Running out to Trader Joe's or Aldi for low-carb bread adds up fast, but whipping up a batch of this takes about ten minutes of active work and pennies per round. When I first tested this recipe, I learned the hard way that skipping the cream of tartar leaves you with a sad, watery puddle instead of a sturdy, pillowy mound. You need those stiff peaks to trap the air before it hits the sheet pan at 300°F. It is completely gluten-free, surprisingly filling, and makes the best base for a quick morning avocado toast or turkey sandwich when you are trying to cut back on grocery spending.
ingredients: 3 large eggs, separated into whites and yolks
3 tbsp plain cream cheese, softened to room temperature (Kirkland brand works great)
1/4 tsp cream of tartar (do not skip this or the whites won't hold)
Optional: 1/4 tsp garlic powder or everything bagel seasoning for topping
instructions: Preheat your oven to 300°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper, giving it a very light spray of oil so the rounds peel off easily later.

In a clean glass bowl, beat the egg whites and cream of tartar with an electric hand mixer on medium-high speed until stiff, glossy peaks form that hold their shape when you lift the beaters straight up.

In a separate small bowl, whisk the egg yolks and softened cream cheese together until completely smooth and free of lumps, then gently fold this mixture into the whipped egg whites using a rubber spatula until just combined without deflating the air.
Spoon the batter into 6 equal mounds on your prepared baking sheet, gently smoothing the tops into flat circles about 3 inches wide and half an inch thick.
Bake on the middle rack for 18 to 20 minutes until the edges turn a light golden brown and the tops spring back slightly when touched, then let them cool completely on the pan before peeling.
proHack: Make sure your mixing bowl is 100% oil-free. Even a microscopic speck of grease or egg yolk will stop your egg whites from whipping into those critical stiff peaks.
servingIdea: Pile high with sliced deli turkey, sharp cheddar from Aldi, crisp romaine lettuce, and a smear of yellow mustard for a zero-carb lunch sandwich.
storage: Store leftover cloud bread in an airtight container in the fridge with a paper towel to absorb moisture for up to 3 days, or freeze them flat between sheets of parchment paper for up to a month. Reheat straight from frozen in a toaster oven on low heat.

faqs.question: Can I use cottage cheese instead of cream cheese?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you will need to blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth first so you do not end up with grainy egg whites.

faqs.question: Why did my cloud bread deflate in the oven?
faqs.answer: Over-mixing the batter is usually the culprit. Fold the yolk mixture into the whites as gently as possible using broad, sweeping strokes.
